plan.notes: Source: Bronx Community College (CUNY) official "Degree Map: BUSINESS ADMINISTRATION, Computer Programming Option, A.S. Degree", Revised 06/2023 (bcc.cuny.edu). The map is a recommended semester-by-semester sequence; its own disclaimer says it is for advisement and degree requirements are in the college catalog. Credit reconciliation (honest, footnote-driven): the map declares semester subtotals 13-14 / 16 / 16 / 15 and TOTAL 60-61. Semester I transcribes FYS 11 at its 1-credit freshman-track value (map lists 0-1; footnote 3 waives it only for students entering with 24+ degree/equated credits, who then need only 60 credits) -> 14. Semester III transcribes the Life and Physical Science slot at 4 credits (map lists 3-4; footnote 5 requires a 3-credit selection to be paired with an additional 1-credit lab, so the graduation-relevant minimum is 4) -> 16. Result: 14+16+16+15 = 61, within the map's published TOTAL 60-61 and equal to the freshman-track total; every semester sum matches the map's declared subtotal at the chosen values. REMEDIAL SEQUENCE rows are excluded (remedial, non-degree credit). Prerequisites recorded only where the map prints them (MTH 30 requires MTH 28 or equivalent; DAT 47 requires DAT 10 or DAT 30 or departmental approval; DAT 49 requires DAT 30 or departmental approval; DAT 51 requires BIS 13 and DAT 30, or departmental approval). Course titles and credit values verified against the map text; "or" alternates folded into choice slots with options. Filed as catalog year 2023-2024 per the 06/2023 revision; the map itself carries no explicit catalog year, disclosed here. Graduation also requires all required courses with appropriate grades, two writing-intensive courses, minimum GPA 2.0, and a graduation application (per the map note).

courses.title: English Composition I (Required Core A): ENG 100 OR ENG 110 OR ENG 111
courses.choice_note: Map literal: "Required Core A: English Composition I - ENG 100 Integrated Reading and Writing OR ENG 110 Fundamentals of Writing and Rhetoric OR ENG 111 Writing and Rhetoric". Per footnote 1, placement depends on English Proficiency Index (ENG 100 with EPI 0-49, ENG 110 with EPI 50-64, ENG 111 with EPI 65+).

courses.title: College Algebra and Trigonometry (Required Core B): MTH 28 or MTH 28.5
courses.choice_note: Map literal: "Required Core B: MTH 28 College Algebra and Elementary Trigonometry OR MTH 28.5 College Algebra and Elementary Trigonometry Corequisite". Per footnote 2, students eligible for MTH 28 enroll in MTH 28; others take the MTH 28.5 corequisite version.

courses.title: First Year Seminar
courses.choice_note: Map lists FYS 11 as 0-1 credit; transcribed at the 1-credit freshman-track value. Per footnote 3, the requirement is waived for students who have earned 24+ degree or equated credits (transfer students), who then complete only 60 credits to graduate. Highly recommended in the first or second semester before earning 24 credits.

courses.title: Composition and Rhetoric II (Required Core A): ENG 112 OR ENG 113 OR ENG 114 OR ENG 115 OR ENG 116
courses.choice_note: Map literal: "Required Core A: ENG 112 Composition and Rhetoric II OR ENG 113 Writing About Literature OR ENG 114 Written Composition and Prose Fiction OR ENG 115 Written Composition and Drama OR ENG 116 Written Composition and Poetry".

courses.title: Flexible Core A-D: Select ONE course from any Flexible Core Area
courses.choice_note: Map literal. Per footnote 4, to select courses accepted as transfer credits at senior colleges and give breadth nationally required of business majors, students are strongly recommended to complete HIS 10 or HIS 11 and/or COMM 34 to fulfill Flexible Core A; ECO 12 to fulfill Flexible Core B; and COMM 11 and/or ECO 11 to fulfill Flexible Core D.

courses.title: Life and Physical Science (Required Core C)
courses.choice_note: Map literal: "Required Core C: Select ONE course from Life and Physical Science", listed at 3-4 credits. Per footnote 5, a 3-credit selection must be paired with an additional 1-credit lab to fulfill graduation requirements, so the graduation-relevant value is 4 credits; transcribed at 4.
